newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Creditors settle over Pyramid group collapse.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Creditors settle over Pyramid group collapse.

text.p: Creditors of the collapsed Pyramid group of building societies announced on Thursday they had reached a settlement with group's liquidator, ending a six-year dispute.
The Pyramid group collapsed in 1990, owing 10,000 non-withdrawable shareholders a total of A$124 million.
The Victoria state government is also a major creditor, after it intervened during the collapse to bail out depositors.

Liquidator Ferrier Hodgson said in a statement that it, the government and the shareholders had reached a settlement but declined to give details until the Supreme Court in Melbourne approved the agreement at a hearing late next month.

Pyramid, a casualty of the 1980s debt binge, spawned Australia's largest ever civil case as non-withdrawable shareholders, a class of equity deemed to rank alongside debt, fought for a share of the liquidated assets.
